title: Dates past 9999 and before year 1; out-of-range days panic
verdict: no `date_range` limit; `Int32` days beyond chrono's range panic
description: Date arithmetic is not limited to 0001-01-01 … 9999-12-31: one day before 0001-01-01 is 0000-12-31 and one after 9999-12-31 is +10000-01-01; timestamps (microseconds) reach year 12736 and beyond.

A date is an `Int32` of days, wider than chrono's `NaiveDate` (about ±262 000 years). Casting such a day count to `Date` succeeds, `dt.year()` of it is NULL, and turning it into text or a Python value panics (`PanicException: out-of-range date`, PL-2).

provenance.notes: `sverify_dev.probe_polars` runs each expression on edge cases (0, ±1, ±2, 3, ±7, the bounds of the integer width; 0.5, ±2.5, 7, 1e308, ±inf, NaN; NULL), one row at a time, and compares each row with Lean's outcome of the Substrait call under each candidate option (`substrait-check --outcomes`). Observations are Polars programs whose result is recorded as it is. Polars 2.1.0 (Python), Rust crates at tag py-2.1.0 (commit 7f902bd3), on macOS arm64.
